public_rationale: The retrieved evidence does not settle the three-part claim. Earlier medical research documents important limitations, while writing research shows that quality judgments can favor AI under some conditions. Neither establishes full-job capability at publication. The accounting evidence is incomplete. Failure to find a verified replacement cannot prove that replacement was impossible, and narrow task successes cannot prove that a whole job was replaceable.
limitations: All cited findings are context rather than direct outcome evidence for the June 16 snapshot.
The ordinary reading of good writing still requires an explicit evaluator choice.
The three professions should not receive a common definitive verdict based on evidence about only one.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Current AI cannot replace an accountant or a doctor, and cannot replace a writer if good writing is wanted.
conditions: writer: if good writing is wanted

statement.excerpt: Can you replace an accountant? No. A doctor? No. A writer? Not if you want good writing.

from_speaker: Can you replace an accountant? No.
A writer? Not if you want good writing.
our_interpretation: Replace means sustain the core duties of an actual job without another professional doing those duties in the AI's place. It does not require replacing every member of the profession.
Good writing means competent work fit for its intended professional purpose, rather than an evaluator's personal literary taste.
The reference to technology that exists today fixes the capability snapshot at June 16, 2025.
Task scores, assistance to an employed professional, and licensing-exam performance are insufficient by themselves to establish full-job replacement.
criteria.support_condition: Credible evaluations covering the essential duties of all three job categories establish that available systems could not reliably replace the worker, including professional-quality writing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A verified sustained deployment or comprehensive evaluation demonstrates replacement of at least one named job category using technology available by publication; assess the remaining categories separately.

evidence.explanation: The study identifies shortcomings in autonomous clinical decisions using a simulated setting built from patient cases. It does not establish the performance of all systems available on June 16, 2025, or assess every duty of a doctor.

evidence.locator: Abstract, sentence contrasting non-expert and expert ratings
evidence.explanation: The revised paper reports differing assessments of short-story creativity, with non-experts more favorable to model outputs than experts. This challenges a blanket dismissal of AI writing quality but does not demonstrate replacement of a professional writer; the experiment's exact date is not supplied on the abstract page.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Version-dated, comprehensive professional evaluations or sustained deployments of systems available by June 16, 2025, documenting the full duties performed, human intervention, and output quality for each profession.
